beats.lead: The bikeshedding story usually stops after two items on the agenda.
beats.text: A committee approves a nuclear reactor in minutes, then burns 45 minutes arguing over a bike shed.
beats.note: There was a third item on that same 1957 agenda, and almost nobody quotes it.

beats.name: Parkinson's Law, and Other Studies in Administration
beats.role: C. Northcote Parkinson invented a fictional finance committee to make the point — not a real boardroom, a chapter called 'High Finance, or the Point of Vanishing Interest.'

beats.lead: The famous half of the story checks out.
beats.text: A GBP 10 million reactor contract: passed in two and a half minutes. A GBP 350 bike shed: 45 minutes of debate.
beats.note: Everyone could picture a bike shed, so everyone had an opinion on the roofing material.

beats.context: How long that same committee then argued over the GBP 21 annual coffee budget — longer than the bike shed, and Parkinson has them still undecided when the meeting ends.

beats.name: Poul-Henning Kamp
beats.role: The word 'bikeshedding' itself is his, not Parkinson's — a FreeBSD mailing-list email sent 2 October, after weeks of argument over a genuinely simple patch to add fractional seconds to the sleep command.

beats.line: The trivial item was never the bike shed. It was whatever's easiest to have an opinion on.
